process_conclusion: The selector is behaviourally a no-op on the current LEARNING_PROCESS queue modulo an arbitrary task_id tiebreak (P-001 chosen either way; P-003/P-004 swap only on tied benefit fields). It reorders HIGHER_ORDER candidates substantively (R-003 above R-005). No campaign outcome data exists to show that either reordering improved information flow, so no selector advantage is demonstrated.

Equivalent (verbatim) experiments are not repeated: every resolved frontier cell maps to exactly one executed check + one artifact, and no task has been selected twice. Near-duplicate parameter extensions do occur: (A) the cross-sectional construction was executed at lookback 20 (FALSIFIED) and again at lookback 63 (FALSIFIED) even though the 20-day cell's perturbation sweep already covered lookbacks 10/20/40, and (B) a superseded 3/5/10/20 momentum lookback sweep (momentum_sweep.py) coexists with the retained 3/5/10 sweep (momentum_lookback_sweep.py). Both near-duplicates were low-cost and produced corroborating, independently verified FALSIFIED evidence, and neither blocked search redirection. The controller queue has no checkable novelty guard, but the observed near-duplicates arose at authoring time (new check files), not at queue selection, so a queue-level guard alone would not have caught them.
research_conclusion: SUPPORTED (cost-robust). The predeclared cost grid shows the short-horizon momentum edge survives conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected universe: 9/10 assets retain a strictly positive net-of-cost per-segment median at every cost level and lookback, the zero-cost column reproduces momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json exactly, and the full-sample realized cost drag is ~1.1% (realistic) / ~2.2% (2x conservative). The sole non-survivor (NVDA) was already non-positive at zero cost and is cost-fragile. The candidate momentum admission therefore remains qualified as cost-robust; the cost qualification that motivated this task is closed.
